findings.issue: The new 'Lockout during a lock' note is accurate: no single lock can be extended. The unchanged 'Victim DoS' bullet still says the lock is 'capped at 15 m, never permanent', and that overstates the bound. Only recordSuccess resets failedAttempts (UserCredential.java:126-129). It stays at or above the threshold after locked_until passes, so a single wrong OTP right after expiry starts a new 15 m lock (overshoot keeps it at max-duration). An attacker who knows the victim's verified phone can still keep password and OTP login locked indefinitely with about 4 requests an hour. The password path behaves the same way, so this is the same residual risk in both paths, and the delta does not make it worse. The second half of my round-1 doc fix was not applied.
findings.fix: Reword the Victim DoS bullet, for example: 'each lock lasts at most 15 m, but a persistent attacker can start a new lock after each expiry (one wrong attempt per 15 m)'. Optionally track decaying failedAttempts after expiry as a backlog item.

findings.issue: The response body and status are identical whether or not the account is locked: both return AUTH_OTP_INVALID, and the new IT asserts this through wrongOtp. Wall-clock time can differ, though. When the account is unlocked, a wrong code also runs the REQUIRES_NEW recordFailure transaction (read plus UPDATE). When it is locked, that write is skipped. That gives a small timing signal for lock state. The value is low, because the attacker usually caused the lock and the password path already reveals lock state outright. Separately, isLocked and recordFailure are check-then-act, so concurrent wrong codes at the threshold can extend a fresh lock once. That is bounded and negligible.
findings.fix: Accept and add one line to the existing 'Residual timing risk' bullet. No code change needed.

summary: Delta 2a745cb3..fca9bc19 closes the round-1 lock-renewal minor. OtpLoginService.verify only calls loginAttempts.recordFailure when isLocked(userId) is false, so a wrong OTP during an active lock writes nothing. OtpLockoutIT.wrongOtpsDoNotRenewLock asserts that locked_until and failed_attempts do not change, and that every attempt still returns AUTH_OTP_INVALID. This matches the password path (LoginService catches LockedException before recordFailure). No response oracle is introduced. Wrong codes return the same AUTH_OTP_INVALID whether or not the account is locked, AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED is still returned only after a correct code, and unknown and unverified phones still record nothing. The only difference is the minor timing signal described above. The doc changes are accurate. The OTP caps are incremented in request() before issueCode applies the 30 s resend cooldown, so they count requests. The refresh limiter now runs through the shared Redis counter. The Redis TTL and eviction note and the fallback-map wholesale-clear note correctly close my round-1 minors 3 and 4 as documented soft controls. The new 'cannot renew a lock' note is correct, but the Victim DoS bullet still overstates the bound, because one wrong attempt after each expiry starts a new lock. Nothing else new is introduced. The Javadoc edits only drop the Bucket4j references. The SharedWindowCounterTest timeout bound was tightened from 5 s to 1 s, which affects only tests; it could be flaky on slow CI but has no security impact. No endpoint, auth, role, /internal/**, dependency, logging or PII changes. The add-phone SMS-pumping item stays in the backlog and the delta does not make it worse.
